parsing_res_list.block_content: ## Appendix D Proof of the Main Theorem
Proof of Theorem 4. First we use the set  $ X_0 $ from Proposition 8. Take arbitrary  $ x \in X_0 $ and an affine hyperplane  $ H = \{l = 0\} $.

Idea of the proof. We prove by contradiction. Assume that for the chosen  $ x \in X_0 $ and  $ H $ the fraction of time in  $ U_\varepsilon(H) $ does not tend to zero as  $ \varepsilon \to 0 $. For a chosen small  $ \delta $ we partition time into blocks. In each block the time in  $ U_\varepsilon(H) $ is split into two parts:
$$ \mathrm{(i)~inside~W_{\delta},\qquad(ii)~outside~W_{\delta}.} $$

For the first part we already have a small average estimate from Step 0. For the second part we need to show that for sufficiently small  $ \varepsilon $ the average time outside  $ W_{\delta} $ can also be made arbitrarily small.
Step 1: choice of  $ \delta $. Assume the contrary: there exist  $ \gamma > 0 $ and a sequence  $ \varepsilon_k \to 0 $ such that
$$ \limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbf{1}_{U_{\varepsilon_{k}}(H)}(\Phi^{t}x)dt\geq\gamma. $$
By the definition of  $ X_{0} $ we can choose  $ \delta > 0 $ so that
$$ b_{\delta}(x)=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbf{1}_{W_{\delta}}(\Phi^{t}x)dt<\frac{\gamma^{2}}{64}. $$
For this δ we further fix the exit time estimate from Lemma 10 and the constant cδ from Lemma 9.
Step 2: blocks and bad blocks. Choose the block length  $ T_{0} = 1 $. Consider a large time  $ T = mT_{0} $. The number T is chosen large enough so that the average
$$ \frac{1}{T}\int_{0}^{T}\mathbf{1}_{W_{\delta}}(\Phi^{t}x)dt $$
is sufficiently close to its limit from (16). Partition  $ [0, mT_{0}] $ into blocks
Denote the fraction of time in  $ W_{\delta} $ inside a block by
$$ v_{j}=\frac{1}{T_{0}}\int_{I_{j}}\mathbf{1}_{W_{\delta}}(\Phi^{t}x)d t, $$
and the fraction of time in  $ U_{\varepsilon}(H) $ by
$$ w_{j}=\frac{1}{T_{0}}\int_{I_{j}}\mathbf{1}_{U_{\varepsilon}(H)}(\Phi^{t}x)d t. $$
We call a block  $ I_j $ bad if  $ v_j \geq \gamma/8 $.
Since  $ x \in X_0 $, for the chosen  $ \delta $ we have
$$ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}v_{j}<\frac{\gamma^{2}}{64}. $$
